title: Inspect the Ticket Inbox
subtitle: Tag the fields triage runs on
scenario: It is 2:05 PM at Relay's support desk. A ticket just landed and the clock is running - misroute it and a customer outage sits in the wrong inbox. Before you classify anything, read the raw ticket like an automation designer and tag the fields triage depends on. Watch the customer's guess: what they think is wrong is not the same as the symptom.
input: TKT-4001 | Channel: email | From: acme-corp | Product: Checkout | "Checkout is down for all our users - nobody can pay. Maybe a billing problem on your end?" | Received: 2:05 PM.
instructions: Read the ticket as a source, not as data to classify yet.
Tag the ticket id, channel, and product area to their spans.
Tag the SYMPTOM the customer reports - not the cause they guess.
Validate to mint the ticket source profile.

segments.text: Checkout is down for all users

fields.label: Ticket id
fields.explain: The ticket id (TKT-####) is the key every triage step joins on - tag the identifier, not the timestamp.

fields.label: Channel
fields.explain: Tag how the ticket arrived (email); the channel is provenance, not the product it is about.

fields.label: Product area
fields.explain: Tag the product area the ticket is about (Checkout), which anchors classification and routing.

fields.label: Reported symptom
fields.explain: Tag what is actually happening - checkout is down - not the customer's guessed cause ('maybe a billing problem').

artifactOnPass.symptom: Checkout is down for all users

successMessage: Ticket profiled. You separated the symptom from the customer's guess - next, build the ticket record.

intro.heading: Before you triage: read the ticket

sections.title: Triage fails at the inputs
sections.body: Most misroutes start with a misread ticket. Before classifying, a designer profiles the source: the id to join on, the channel it came from, the product it touches, and the real symptom.

sections.title: Symptom, not the customer's cause
sections.body: Customers guess. 'Maybe a billing problem' is a guess; 'checkout is down' is the symptom. Tagging the symptom - what is observably happening - is what keeps classification honest.

sections.title: Volume needs structure
sections.body: A support desk sees this all day. Turning each free-text ticket into a few tagged fields is what makes triage automatable instead of an inbox someone reads by hand.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A ticket source profile the record is keyed from - proof the ticket is understood before any category is assigned.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd skim the ticket and jot the id, channel, product, and what is actually broken - ignoring the customer's guess at the cause.

tools.powerAutomate: an Outlook/helpdesk trigger mapping ticket fields into variables
tools.zapier: a 'New ticket' trigger pulling id, channel, and body
tools.python: parse the ticket payload into id, channel, product, symptom

takeaway.heading: Ticket profiled
points: You tagged the id, channel, and product area triage joins on.
You tagged the reported symptom, not the customer's guessed cause.
